title: Spin-wave circulation in unbounded ferromagnetic film
authors: Jan Klima, Daniel Stoeffler, Andres Sarmiento, Kevin Weber, Loic Temdie, Aurélie Solignac, Roberto Fenollosa, Yves Henry, Matthieu Bailleul, Vincent Vlaminck
abstract: A key challenge in spin-wave computing is steering spin waves through circuits without wave distortion or reflections. This often results in 1D propagation scenarios, which hinder applicability in 2D magnonic circuits. We demonstrate experimentally a novel approach using a hard magnetic spherical microparticle to guide spin-waves onto a closed path in a plain thin YIG film. The particle stray field induces a radially symmetrical magnetization landscape, which allows spin-waves to loop around. In parallel, we conducted micromagnetic simulations reproducing the experimental conditions, which confirm the circulation of spin-waves over several loops around the particle. This work demonstrates the possibility to steer spin-waves onto a circular path using inhomogeneous magnetic landscape, as well as advancing scalable spin-wave-based information processing technologies.
summary: This paper presents an experimental and simulation study demonstrating a novel method to guide spin waves around a closed loop in a thin YIG film using a hard magnetic microparticle. By creating a controlled, inhomogeneous magnetic landscape, the authors successfully achieve spin-wave circulation, advancing the feasibility of 2D magnonic information processing circuits.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is steering spin waves onto a closed path in thin films to overcome the limitations of 1D propagation in magnonic circuits.
main_result: The authors experimentally and numerically demonstrate that using a hard magnetic microparticle to create a radially symmetrical magnetization landscape allows for stable, measurable circulation of spin waves around the particle.
method: The work combines experimental measurements using Vector Network Analyzers (VNA) on YIG films with detailed micromagnetic simulations (Mumax3) to model the magnetic dynamics.
model_or_system: The physical system is an unbounded thin YIG film subjected to the stray field of a hard magnetic spherical microparticle. The simulation models the resulting inhomogeneous magnetization landscape and the subsequent spin-wave dynamics.
key_observables: Spin wave transmission parameters ($S_{12}, S_{21}$), time-of-flight delays corresponding to multiple loops, and the evolution of magnetic flux ($\Phi(m_z)$).
important_parameters: Particle height ($z$), magnetic remanence ($\mu_0M_r$), and the resulting curvature radius of the spin-wave trajectory.
main_assumptions: The non-reciprocity observed is attributed to chirality, and the analysis relies on the particle's stray field creating the necessary radial magnetic profile.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup, the simulated radial magnetization profile, and time-domain/FFT analysis showing spin-wave packets corresponding to multiple loops around the particle.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the 1D propagation limitation to presenting the experimental setup and measurements, followed by detailed micromagnetic simulations that confirm the looping behavior and analyze the complex radiation patterns.
why_interesting: While focused on classical magnonics, the study of wave propagation in highly structured, inhomogeneous media, and the analysis of wave caustics and non-reciprocity, touches upon concepts relevant to wave physics in open quantum systems and engineered photonic/magnonic circuits.
